info.title: Lithica
info.description:
The API of Lithica, a self-hosted image board.

How the API works (authentication, file uploads, errors, field selection,
versioning, what the resources mean and the search syntax) is explained in
`doc/API.md` of the source. This document is the reference of the endpoints.

Every request must send `Accept: application/json`. A request may be
anonymous; what it is allowed to do then is set by the privileges in the
server's configuration.

get.description:
Retrieves simple statistics. `<featured-post>` is null if there is no
featured post yet. `<server-time>` is pretty much the same as the `Date`
HTTP field, only formatted in a manner consistent with other dates. Values
in `config` key are taken directly from the server config, with the
exception of privilege array keys being converted to lower camel case to
match the API convention.

`<modules>` are the names of the optional modules this server has switched
on, in the order of its configuration; empty on a plain installation. A
module's routes are under `modules/<name>/`.

`<max-upload-size>` is the largest request the server takes, in bytes, and
`<accepted-types>` the types of file a post can be made from here (the
engine's, then those of the modules switched on), each with its MIME
type(s) and usual extensions: hints for a client, to point out at once a
file that would be refused. The server still decides by the file's
content.

`<disk-usage>` is the size of the data directory. It is measured in the
background and can be up to an hour old; it is null until the first
measurement after a server start has finished. When several server processes
run, each measures for itself, so two requests can briefly report different
sizes.

post.description:
Creates a new user using specified parameters. Names and passwords must
match `user_name_regex` and `password_regex` from server's configuration,
respectively. Email address, rank and avatar fields are optional. Avatar
style can be either `gravatar` or `manual`. `manual` avatar style requires
client to pass also `avatar` file - see file uploads for details. If the
rank is empty and the user happens to be the first user ever created, become
an administrator, whereas subsequent users will be given the rank indicated
by `default_rank` in the server's configuration.

Errors:

- a user with such name already exists (names are case insensitive)
- either user name, password, email or rank are invalid
- the user is trying to update their or someone else's rank to higher than
  their own
- avatar is missing for manual avatar style
- privileges are too low

get.description:
Sends a confirmation email to given user. The email contains link containing
a token. The token cannot be guessed, thus using such link proves that the
person who requested to reset the password also owns the mailbox, which is a
strong indication they are the rightful owner of the account.

The token is random, works once and expires after the time set in
`password_reset_token_lifetime` (one hour by default). Requesting another
email makes the previous token stop working.

The answer is the same 200 `{}` whether the account exists, has an email
or not, and whether a mail was sent: it does not tell who has an account
on the site. The mail goes out after the answer. An account is sent at
most one mail per `password_reset_mail_interval` (five minutes by
default); a request sooner sends nothing and leaves the link already
sent working.

Errors:

- the site cannot send mail (no mail server is set up): 500
  `MailNotConfiguredError`; `canSendMails` of `GET /info` says so ahead

post.description:
Creates a new tag using specified parameters. Names, suggestions and
implications must match `tag_name_regex` from server's configuration.
Category must exist and is the same as `name` field within `<tag-category>`
resource. Suggestions and implications are optional. If specified implied
tags or suggested tags do not exist yet, they will be automatically created.
Tags created automatically have no implications, no suggestions, one name
and their category is set to the first tag category found. If there are no
tag categories established yet, an error will be thrown.

Errors:

- any name is used by an existing tag (names are case insensitive)
- any name, implication or is invalid
- category is invalid
- no name was specified
- implications or suggestions contain any item from names (e.g. there's a
  shallow cyclic dependency)
- privileges are too low

post.description:
Creates a new post. If specified tags do not exist yet, they will be
automatically created. Tags created automatically have no implications, no
suggestions, one name and their category is set to the first tag category
found. Safety must be any of `"safe"`, `"sketchy"` or `"unsafe"`. Relations
must contain valid post IDs. If `<flag>` is omitted, they will be defined by
default (`"loop"` will be set for all video posts, and `"sound"` will be
auto-detected). Sending empty `thumbnail` will cause the post to use default
thumbnail. If `anonymous` is set to truthy value, the uploader name won't be
recorded (privilege verification still applies; it's possible to disallow
anonymous uploads completely from config.) For details on how to pass
`content` and `thumbnail`, see file uploads.

Errors:

- tags have invalid names
- safety, notes or flags are invalid
- relations refer to non-existing posts
- privileges are too low

get.summary: Get the content extracted from a post's file
get.description:
Retrieves what the modules of this installation read out of the post's
file: metadata embedded in it, such as PNG text chunks or EXIF. There is
one result per piece of content found, and a post may have several of
one kind. What `content` holds depends on the kind and is described by
the module that owns it. The kinds a post has are listed in the
`contentKinds` field of the post.

Without modules, and for a post in which nothing was found, the list is
empty. A module can mark parts of its content as private; those are left
out unless the requester has the `posts:view:content:private` privilege.

Errors:

- the post does not exist
- privileges are too low

and comments to the target post. If `replaceContent` is set to true, content
of the target post is replaced using the content of the source post;

source, whether to loop the video and other scalar values do not get
transferred and are discarded.

get.summary: Get the character card of a post
get.description:
Returns the character card of a post, read for a viewer: the same fields
for every version of the card format (V1, V2, V3) and for both files a
card comes in (PNG, CHARX). Every field is present; a text the card does
not have is empty, and a lorebook it does not have is `null`.

The card as its file had it is the post's extracted content,
`GET /post/<id>/content`.

Errors:

- the post does not exist
- the post has no character card
- privileges are too low

get.summary: Download the character card of a post
get.description:
Returns the file of a post that has a character card, unchanged: the PNG
picture or the CHARX file that was uploaded. It is sent as an attachment
named after the character, with the extension of the stored file
(`Content-Disposition`, with `filename*` for a name that is not ASCII),
or `card-<post id>` where the card's name cannot be a file name.

Unlike the rest of the API, this route answers with the file, so a
request does not have to accept JSON; its errors are JSON all the same.

Errors:

- the post does not exist
- the post has no character card, or its file is missing
- privileges are too low
